s0401.literal: Prince of Wu Commandery Fan, styled Chengguang, was Houzhu's tenth son.
s0401.idiomatic: Prince of Wu Commandery Fan, styled Chengguang, was Houzhu's tenth son.

s0402.literal: In Zhenming year 2 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu Commandery.
s0402.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 2 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu Commandery.

s0403.literal: In year 3 he entered the Pass.
s0403.idiomatic: In year 3 he entered the Pass.

s0404.literal: Under the Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Fucheng.
s0404.idiomatic: Under the Sui's Daye era he was magistrate of Fucheng.

s0405.literal: Prince of Qiantang Tian, styled Chengtan, was Houzhu's eleventh son.
s0405.idiomatic: Prince of Qiantang Tian, styled Chengtan, was Houzhu's eleventh son.

s0406.literal: In Zhenming year 2 he was established as Prince of Qiantang, with a fief of one thousand households.
s0406.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 2 he was established as Prince of Qiantang, with a fief of one thousand households.

s0407.literal: In year 3 he entered the Pass and died at Chang'an.
s0407.idiomatic: In year 3 he entered the Pass and died at Chang'an.

s0408.literal: From the Eastern Jin onward in the Jiang region, when princes opened their states, household counts determined the three grades of large, medium, and small.
s0408.idiomatic: From the Eastern Jin onward south of the Yangtze, when princes opened their states, household counts set the three grades—large, medium, and small.

s0409.literal: Large states had upper, middle, and lower generals and one marshal;
s0409.idiomatic: Large states had upper, middle, and lower generals and one marshal;

s0410.literal: medium states had middle and lower generals;
s0410.idiomatic: medium states had middle and lower generals;

s0413.literal: From the Founder's accession through Yongding down to Zhenming, only Prince of Hengyang Chang received exceptional favor, up to five thousand households.
s0413.idiomatic: From the Founder's accession through Yongding to Zhenming, only Prince of Hengyang Chang was favored exceptionally, to five thousand households.

s0414.literal: All other large states had no more than two thousand households; small states had one thousand.
s0414.idiomatic: All other large states had no more than two thousand households; small states had one thousand.

s0415.literal: The old histories are damaged and cannot distinguish each state's household counts; therefore their remnants are appended here.
s0415.idiomatic: The old histories are damaged and cannot distinguish each state's household counts; their remnants are therefore appended here.

s0416.literal: The historian says: Emperor Wen, Emperor Xuan, and Houzhu all erected feudal shields to plant worthy kin, strengthening the root and elevating the foundation stones.
s0416.idiomatic: The historian says: Emperor Wen, Emperor Xuan, and Houzhu all raised feudal screens to plant worthy kin, strengthening the root and elevating the bedrock.

s0417.literal: Prince of Poyang Boshan had presence and virtue and was a worthy prince of the age.
s0417.idiomatic: Prince of Poyang Boshan had presence and virtue and was a worthy prince of his age.

s0418.literal: Prince of Yueyang Shuzhen, at the state's crisis, grieved for house and realm, threw himself wholly against the enemy, with no thought of living.
s0418.idiomatic: Prince of Yueyang Shuzhen, when the altars were tottering, grieved for house and realm, threw himself wholly against the enemy, and did not seek to live.

s0420.literal: In antiquity this is what we mean by dying loyal for the cause.
s0420.idiomatic: In antiquity this is what we mean by dying loyal for the cause.

s0422.literal: [2] Grand Tutor—in the Founder's annals it reads "Grand Commandant."
s0422.idiomatic: On "[2] Grand Tutor": the Founder's annals read Grand Commandant.

s0423.literal: [3] Born knowing filial piety—in all editions "born" reads "sit."
s0423.idiomatic: On "[3] born knowing filial piety": all editions read sit for born.

s0424.literal: [4] From year eleven to advancement as Opening the Government, Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers—according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan, Boshan received Equal in Honor in the first month of the thirteenth year of Taijian.
s0424.idiomatic: On "[4] from year eleven to Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers": Emperor Xuan's annals place Boshan's advancement in the first month of Taijian year 13.

s0425.literal: [6] In year eleven advanced to General Who Guards the Front—according to the Basic Annals, Boxin's advancement was in Houzhu's Zhenming year 1, not in Emperor Xuan's Taijian year 11.
s0425.idiomatic: On "[6] in year eleven advanced to General Who Guards the Front": the Basic Annals place Boxin's advancement in Houzhu's Zhenming year 1, not Emperor Xuan's Taijian year 11.

s0426.literal: [7] Together with Marquis of Linru Fangqing was killed by Wang Yong, Inspector of Eastern Hengzhou—the character "east" was originally an ink dot in the base text; all editions read "west"; according to Fangqing's biography Wang Yong was Inspector of Eastern Hengzhou; one character "east" is now supplied.
s0426.idiomatic: On "[7] killed by Wang Yong, Inspector of Eastern Hengzhou": east was an ink dot in the base text and all editions read west; Fangqing's biography has Wang Yong as inspector of Eastern Hengzhou, so east is restored.

s0428.literal: [8] In year seven transferred to General Who Wins the Championship and Central Leader of the Gentlemen—according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan, Boren as central leader was in the eleventh month of Taijian year 8.
s0428.idiomatic: On "[8] in year seven transferred to General Who Wins the Championship and Central Leader of the Gentlemen": Emperor Xuan's annals place Boren as central leader in the eleventh month of Taijian year 8.

s0429.literal: [9] In Zhenming year 1 made Attendant-in-Ordinary—"attendant-in-ordinary" in Houzhu's annals reads "special advancement."
s0429.idiomatic: On "[9] in Zhenming year 1 made Attendant-in-Ordinary": Houzhu's annals read special advancement for attendant-in-ordinary.

s0430.literal: [10] From early Taijian to Inspector of Hezhou—according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan, Boyi in the seventh month of Taijian year 9 as General of Light Chariots and Administrator of Danyang became Inspector of Hezhou; in the ninth month of year 10 as General Who Propagates Favor became Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou—neither was in early Taijian, and the career shifts do not all match.
s0430.idiomatic: On "[10] from early Taijian to Inspector of Hezhou": Emperor Xuan's annals have Boyi made Hezhou inspector in the seventh month of Taijian year 9 and Eastern Yangzhou inspector in the ninth month of year 10—not early Taijian—and the posts do not all align.

s0431.literal: [11] Censor-in-Chief Xu Junfu memorialized—"Xu Junfu" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Xu Junzheng."
s0431.idiomatic: On "[11] Censor-in-Chief Xu Junfu memorialized": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Xu Junzheng.

s0432.literal: [12] Early famed for heroic plans—in the Southern Supervisory edition "early" reads "from of old"; the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read "formerly."
s0432.idiomatic: On "[12] early famed for heroic plans": the Southern Supervisory edition reads from of old; the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions read formerly.

s0433.literal: [13] Established as Prince of Yongyang in Taijian—according to the imperial annals, establishing Bozhi as Prince of Yongyang was in the second year of Guangda under the deposed emperor, not in Taijian.
s0433.idiomatic: On "[13] established as Prince of Yongyang in Taijian": the annals place establishing Bozhi as Prince of Yongyang in deposed-emperor Guangda year 2, not Taijian.

s0434.literal: [14] Advanced step by step to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing—according to Houzhu's annals, Bozhi in the third month of the year Houzhu succeeded became Director of the Masters of Writing; in the fifth month of Zhide year 2 he was again made Director of the Masters of Writing while serving as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou—both mentions of director lack the character "left."
s0434.idiomatic: On "[14] advanced to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing": Houzhu's annals make Bozhi director of the masters of writing in the third month of his accession year and again in Zhide year 2, fifth month—neither has left.

s0435.literal: [15] Commissioner over Eastern Yang and Feng—"Feng" was originally corrupt as "Cao"; no edition errs; now corrected.
s0435.idiomatic: On "[15] commissioner over Eastern Yang and Feng": Feng was originally written Cao; no edition errs; now corrected.

s0436.literal: According to the second year of Guangda under the deposed emperor, fourth month, Jin'an commandery of Eastern Yangzhou was split off as Fengzhou.
s0436.idiomatic: In deposed-emperor Guangda year 2, fourth month, Jin'an commandery of Eastern Yangzhou was split off as Fengzhou.

s0437.literal: [16] Established as Prince of Guiyang in Taijian—according to the imperial annals, establishing Bomao as Prince of Guiyang was in the seventh month of Guangda year 2 under the deposed emperor, not in Taijian.
s0437.idiomatic: On "[16] established as Prince of Guiyang in Taijian": the annals place establishing Bomao as Prince of Guiyang in deposed-emperor Guangda year 2, seventh month—not Taijian.

s0438.literal: [17] Lady of Bright Talent Wei bore Prince of Jian'an Shuqing—"Lady of Bright Talent Wei" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Lady of Bright Talent Wei [Hua]."
s0438.idiomatic: On "[17] Lady of Bright Talent Wei bore Prince of Jian'an Shuqing": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Lady of Bright Talent Wei Hua.

s0439.literal: [18] Prince of Bashan Shuxiong—"Shuxiong" in Houzhu's annals reads "Shuxiong [Bear]"; see Collation Note 5 in Volume 6.
s0439.idiomatic: On "[18] Prince of Bashan Shuxiong": Houzhu's annals read Shuxiong (Bear); see Collation Note 5 in Volume 6.

s0440.literal: [19] Lady Liu bore Prince of Linjiang Shuxian—"Prince of Linjiang" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "Prince of Linhai"; the History of the Southern Dynasties agrees.
s0440.idiomatic: On "[19] Lady Liu bore Prince of Linjiang Shuxian": the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties read Prince of Linhai.

s0441.literal: According to Houzhu's annals, on bingchen of the second month of Zhide year 4, the emperor's younger brother Shuxian was established as Prince of Linjiang; all editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties agree; none read Prince of Linhai; Prince of Linjiang should stand.
s0441.idiomatic: Houzhu's annals record Shuxian established as Prince of Linjiang on bingchen, second month, Zhide year 4; all editions and the Southern History agree—Linjiang, not Linhai, is correct.

s0444.literal: [Hong]—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
s0444.idiomatic: On "[Hong]": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

s0445.literal: Comment: in the Song engraved edition, to avoid taboo the character "Hong" is always written with a missing stroke and often corrupts as "yin."
s0445.idiomatic: The Song engraved edition, avoiding taboo, writes Hong with a missing stroke, often corrupting to yin.

s0446.literal: Yet this "Hong" probably should follow the History of the Southern Dynasties as "Hong [Vast]," because Prince of Yuzhang Shuying's eldest son was named Hong and should not violate his uncle's name taboo.
s0446.idiomatic: Yet this Hong probably should follow the Southern History as Hong (vast), since Prince of Yuzhang Shuying's eldest son was named Hong and must not violate his uncle's taboo.

s0447.literal: [21] In year 5 advanced to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou—"Southern Yuzhou" in the Annals of Emperor Xuan reads "Southern Xuzhou."
s0447.idiomatic: On "[21] in year 5 advanced to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou": Emperor Xuan's annals read Southern Xuzhou.

s0448.literal: Probably one should follow the annals.
s0448.idiomatic: The annals text is probably correct.

s0449.literal: [22] In year 11 made General Who Guards the Front and Inspector of Jiangzhou—"General Who Guards the Front" should follow the Annals of Emperor Xuan as "General Who Guards the South."
s0449.idiomatic: On "[22] in year 11 made General Who Guards the Front and Inspector of Jiangzhou": Emperor Xuan's annals read General Who Guards the South.

s0450.literal: Comment: the title General Who Guards the Front is used internally and should not crown the post of Jiangzhou inspector.
s0450.idiomatic: General Who Guards the Front is an inner-court rank and should not head the Jiangzhou inspectorate.

s0451.literal: [23] In year 4 advanced to Cavalry General-in-Chief—this character "grand" is suspected as a spurious addition.
s0451.idiomatic: On "[23] in year 4 advanced to Cavalry General-in-Chief": the character grand is probably spurious.

s0453.literal: [24] That year transferred to Minister of Works—"Minister of Works" in Houzhu's annals reads "Minister over the Masses."
s0453.idiomatic: On "[24] that year transferred to Minister of Works": Houzhu's annals read Minister over the Masses.

s0454.literal: [25] Soon made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hezhou—according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan, Shujian as Inspector of Hezhou with advancement to General Who Pacifies the North was in the sixth month of Taijian year 8.
s0454.idiomatic: On "[25] soon made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hezhou": Emperor Xuan's annals place Shujian's Hezhou inspectorship and advancement in the sixth month of Taijian year 8.

s0455.literal: [26] Entered court as General of the Left Guard and Administrator of Danyang—according to Houzhu's annals, when Houzhu succeeded, Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Front Guard and Administrator of Danyang Prince of Changsha Shujian was made Cavalry General-in-Chief, Opening the Government, Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, and Inspector of Yangzhou.
s0455.idiomatic: On "[26] entered court as General of the Left Guard and Administrator of Danyang": Houzhu's annals make Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Front Guard, and Danyang administrator Prince of Changsha Shujian cavalry general-in-chief with equal honor and Yangzhou inspector.

s0456.literal: "General of the Left Guard" should read "General of the Front Guard."
s0456.idiomatic: General of the Left Guard should read General of the Front Guard.

s0457.literal: [27] That day captured his generals Dai
s0457.idiomatic: [27] That day captured his generals Dai

s0459.literal: [Wen] and Tan Qilin and the rest—changed according to the Southern Supervisory edition.
s0459.idiomatic: On "[Wen] and Tan Qilin and the rest": emended per the Southern Supervisory edition.

s0460.literal: Comment: the Comprehensive Mirror for Emperor Xuan of Chen, Taijian year 14, also reads "Dai Wen."
s0460.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Emperor Xuan Taijian year 14, also reads Dai Wen.

s0461.literal: [28] Soon restored as Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard—according to Houzhu's annals, Shujian as Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard was in the seventh month of Zhide year 2.
s0461.idiomatic: On "[28] soon restored as Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard": Houzhu's annals place this in the seventh month of Zhide year 2.

s0462.literal: [29] [Shu]xian had always been noble—supplemented according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
s0462.idiomatic: On "[29] [Shu]xian had always been noble": restored per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

s0463.literal: Comment: Shujian changed his name to Shuxian to avoid the taboo on Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian.
s0463.idiomatic: Shujian renamed himself Shuxian to avoid taboo on Sui Emperor Wen Yang Jian.

s0464.literal: [30] Soon made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary through Inspector of Southern Xuzhou—according to the Annals of Emperor Xuan, Shuxian as Inspector of Southern Xuzhou was in the fourth month of Taijian year 12.
s0464.idiomatic: On "[30] soon made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary through Inspector of Southern Xuzhou": Emperor Xuan's annals place Shuxian as Southern Xuzhou inspector in the fourth month of Taijian year 12.

s0465.literal: [31] Advanced to General of Light Chariots and Inspector of Yangzhou—according to Houzhu's annals, Shuwen as Inspector of Yangzhou was in the first month of Zhide year 1.
s0465.idiomatic: On "[31] advanced to General of Light Chariots and Inspector of Yangzhou": Houzhu's annals place Shuwen as Yangzhou inspector in the first month of Zhide year 1.

s0466.literal: [32] Prince of Xinxing Shuchun, styled Zigong—"Zigong" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Zihong."
s0466.idiomatic: On "[32] Prince of Xinxing Shuchun, styled Zigong": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Zihong.

s0467.literal: [33] Prince of Badong Shumo, styled Zigui—Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "'Shumo' is probably 'Shumo [Model],' matching the style name Zigui."
s0467.idiomatic: On "[33] Prince of Badong Shumo, styled Zigui": Zhang Senkai's note says Shumo is probably Shumo (model), matching Zigui.

s0468.literal: [34] Prince of Linjiang Shuxian, styled Ziming—"Ziming" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Ziliang."
s0468.idiomatic: On "[34] Prince of Linjiang Shuxian, styled Ziming": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Ziliang.

s0469.literal: [35] Advanced to General Who Pacifies the South—"General Who Pacifies the South" in Houzhu's annals for Zhenming year 2 reads "General Who Pacifies the North."
s0469.idiomatic: On "[35] advanced to General Who Pacifies the South": Houzhu's annals for Zhenming year 2 read General Who Pacifies the North.

s0470.literal: [36] General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou—"General Who Pacifies the South" in Houzhu's annals for Zhenming year 2 reads "General of Pacified South."
s0470.idiomatic: On "[36] General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou": Houzhu's annals for Zhenming year 2 read General of Pacified South.

s0471.literal: [37] Sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou—"General Who Pacifies the North" in Houzhu's annals reads "General of Pacified North."
s0471.idiomatic: On "[37] sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou": Houzhu's annals read General of Pacified North.

s0472.literal: [38] Under the Sui's Daye era he was
s0472.idiomatic: [38] Under the Sui's Daye era he was

s0474.literal: [Long] magistrate of Chang—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0474.idiomatic: On "[Long] magistrate of Chang": emended per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

s0475.literal: Comment: the Sui Treatises have no Huichang county.
s0475.idiomatic: The Sui Treatises list no Huichang county.
